transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Stone (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Chu (Mariner CTO), Lena Ortiz (Mariner Head of Infra), Marcus Hale (Mariner Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Customer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for payment processing workloads, strict EU data residency (primary region eu-west-1)
- Main concerns: private connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Transit Gateway), cross-account networking, private endpoints, egress controls, KMS integration, SOC2/audit logs, deployment timing
- Next steps: share deployment checklist, network examples, pricing; customer to provide VPC IDs and security contact

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll kick off, Priya our solutions engineer is with me. How are you all?
[00:06] Daniel: Good, thanks. Morning from Dublin. Quick note we're on a bit of a tight timeline — looking at a pilot in Q2, ideally early May.
[00:13] Alex: Great. Today we want to understand your network constraints and security reqs so we can map Redwood Private options — dedicated host or private VPC deployment.
[00:20] Lena: Right. We're mostly focused on Private/VPC deploy. We need everything to stay in eu-west-1, no cross-region replication, and we must integrate with our KMS and SSO.
[00:30] Priya: Got it. Just to clarify, when you say "stay in eu-west-1" do you mean both control plane and data plane? Some customers allow control plane in our managed region but keep data plane in customer's VPC.
[00:45] Marcus: No, both. Legal requires proof data never leaves EU. We also have to be able to audit encryption keys — HSM/KMS integration is important.
[00:54] Alex: Understood. Our Private offering can run with a customer-managed VPC and the data plane stays in your account. We have two common patterns: VPC peering/transit gateway style networking where the Redwood service (or dedicated instances) get routed into your VPC, or AWS PrivateLink-style private endpoints.
[01:12] Daniel: Can you describe the tradeoffs? We're worried about route table complexity and exposure surface.
[01:19] Priya: Sure. With VPC peering or Transit Gateway you get direct routing — lower latency and simple ENI attachment for our pods — but you need to manage route tables and potentially a transit VPC if you have many accounts. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) reduces routing complexity because it's endpoint driven, and it also supports cross-account access without full routing. The caveat: PrivateLink requires ENIs and there's a slight cost increase, and it can be trickier for large-scale egress patterns.
[01:44] Lena: We use a Transit Gateway today for most cross-account services. Could Redwood integrate over TGW?
[01:49] Priya: Yes, we have customers who integrate via TGW. We typically recommend either a dedicated substack that connects to the TGW or PrivateLink depending on your security posture. For strict isolation, PrivateLink + endpoint policies is often preferred.
[02:04] Marcus: Endpoint policies — can we restrict which Redwood endpoints can connect? We don't want open access from the vendor to our whole VPC.
[02:10] Alex: Absolutely, we can bind by account and CIDR, and we support endpoint policies. Also support for security groups to limit traffic to specific ports.
[02:16] Daniel: What about DNS? We run internal Route53 private zones. Will the private endpoints resolve internally?
[02:22] Priya: Yes, with interface endpoints you get private DNS that can be enabled. With peering you'll need to add zone delegation or DNS forwarding; peering doesn't automatically enable private zone resolution across accounts. We've seen customers use Route53 Resolver for that.
[02:35] Marcus: Breaking out, what about egress? We want all outbound traffic to go through our NVA and be logged.
[02:42] Priya: If you have Transit Gateway with centralized egress, we can route our subnets through your TGW and egress will follow your flow. For PrivateLink, egress from our service back to you is via the interface endpoint into your VPC — outbound internet from our side is controlled by us but data plane traffic for inference will remain in your VPC unless you choose a hosted proxy. We can provide docs on how to force egress through your NVA.
[03:04] Daniel: Is there any component that would attempt outbound connections to Redwood-managed control plane?
[03:09] Alex: There is an optional control plane control path; for fully air-gapped/on-prem we have an operator mode, but for most Private deployments the control plane can be in our managed region while data plane stays in your account. If you need everything in your VPC we can discuss an on-prem or fully private control plane bundle, but that's a longer engagement.
[03:29] Lena: For our compliance, we need audit logs sent to our S3 and CloudWatch for retention. Can Redwood ship logs to our S3?
[03:36] Priya: Yes, customers can store audit logs in your S3 bucket via cross-account role, or we can push to your CloudWatch. We'll share the permissions policy.
[03:44] Marcus: KMS integration — we need to use our CMKs and an external HSM. Is that supported?
[03:50] Alex: We support customer-managed KMS keys for storage encryption. HSM integrations are possible for some deployments — we'll need to confirm with infra, but it's in scope for enterprise Private setups. We'll note that as a must-have.
[04:02] Daniel: Latency target — our SLAs for payment auth paths are sub-200ms p95. If we host models in our VPC, is that achievable?
[04:11] Priya: Yes, model latency is mostly local to the data plane. With dedicated GPU pools pinned into your account, we see single-digit to low-double-digit ms for token generation in typical setups. The bigger factor is model selection and sequence length. We'll run benchmarks during the pilot.
[04:25] Alex: We'll propose a small benchmark run using a representative model and your traffic profile. We'll need API keys, a test VPC, and some sample traffic.
[04:33] Daniel: Ok. Also curious about upgrade/rollout — how are model rollouts handled without downtime?
[04:39] Priya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. In Private mode we can run blue/green inside your VPC or use in-place upgrades with load balancing. We'll detail the process in the checklist.
[04:51] Marcus: Any dependencies on specific instance types? We use a mix of c7g and a1 for some services.
[04:57] Priya: For high-performance inference we recommend NVIDIA GPU types or AWS Trainium/Greeanium isn't ideal — (laugh) sorry, Trainium is more for training. We'll share a recommended instance list; options include A10G, A100, L4, and for cost-sensitive workloads we can use quantized CPU paths but that depends on perf tradeoffs. We'll include a mapping.
[05:18] Lena: Network CIDR planning — what subnets do you need?
[05:22] Alex: Typically we ask for one private subnet per AZ with /24s available, security groups to allow inbound from your app subnets, and route table entries to TGW or peering. If using PrivateLink we'll need ENI capacity in the subnet.
[05:34] Daniel: How about cross-account IAM roles? We prefer cross-account role assumption patterns for S3 and KMS.
[05:39] Priya: That's supported. We'll include the role ARNs you'll need to create and the minimum IAM policies.
[05:45] Marcus: From a security compliance view we need SOC2 and pen-test reports, and a contract clause about data processing.
[05:52] Alex: We can share our SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. For contract language we usually offer a BAA or DPA addendum — we'll loop legal.
[06:01] Daniel: Great. Can we get a ballpark of cost for a pilot? We're not ready to commit to dedicated fleet pricing yet.
[06:07] Alex: For a pilot we typically do a short-term reserved for a couple GPUs in your account or a small hosted dedicated pool with burst. We'll send rough pricing ranges — for a small pilot with 2 A10G-equivalent nodes you're looking at X to Y per month (Alex: note to replace with numbers in follow up).
[06:23] Lena: One more operational question: how do we handle secrets and credentials? We want secrets to be stored in our KMS and not passed to Redwood.
[06:30] Priya: You can mount secrets via your KMS or have us reference an encrypted S3 with cross-account access; we don't hold plaintext secrets. We'll include recommended patterns.
[06:40] Daniel: Any gotchas with Route53 resolver endpoint charges or inter-AZ data transfer?
[06:45] Priya: There can be egress costs if traffic crosses AZs or regions; we'll include a cost note. Route53 Resolver endpoints have hourly charges but are common.
[06:53] Marcus: We may need to do a security review with our risk council — can Alex send the SOC2 and network checklist?
[06:59] Alex: Yep. I'll send SOC2, the private deployment checklist, and our network patterns doc. Priya will send network diagrams and the PrivateLink vs Peering decision guide.
[07:09] Daniel: Sounds good. Timeline — pilot in May; security review mid-April?
[07:14] Marcus: Mid-April is fine. We need the docs two weeks prior.
[07:18] Alex: We'll aim to get everything to you by 2026-03-06 so you have time.
[07:22] Priya: Quick clarifying question about region constraints — do you allow any DR outside EU?
[07:27] Lena: No. All copies of customer data must be in eu-west-1. Logs can be mirrored internally but not to non-EU.
[07:33] Priya: Ok we'll mark that as a hard requirement.
[07:37] Daniel: Anything else?
[07:39] Alex: I'll recap next steps — send checklist and SOC2, share pricing, run bench plan. Priya to share network examples. You'll provide VPC IDs and security contacts. We'll schedule a technical deep dive with infra once you share VPC details.
[07:53] Marcus: Good. Also, competitor question — we're evaluating HF endpoints as well, any difference?
[07:58] Priya: Hugging Face endpoints are simpler but don't offer the same managed private deployment and enterprise integrations we provide; also less tuning for production throughput. Anthropic and others are more API-only; for Private VPC we specialize in the orchestration and observability.
[08:13] Daniel: Alright thanks.
[08:15] Alex: Thanks everyone. End notes: shared artifacts — security whitepaper link: https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf, network patterns doc: https://docs.redwood.example.com/private-networking, sample CFN: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-samples/private-cfn.zip

End of call.
